text: Hello everyone, welcome back to our English class.I am Anna.Today we will continue to read the passage, Fishing with Birds.We will discover how the writer describes Daming, the comrades, and the comrades' fishing, and why they are described that way, so that we can understand the writer's attitude and the purpose of writing.Now let's begin with a picture.What is Daming doing?He is cooking with the comrades around him.What's the relationship between Daming and the comrades?Well, some of you may say the comrades are Daming's pets, because Daming takes care of them.Some may think that comrades are Daming's fishing tools, since he uses the birds to catch fish.And some students say that both of them live on fishing, so sometimes they compete for the fish.Very interesting.Everyone has his own understanding.But are they right?We may know the answer after reading the passage in detail.From the passage, we have learned something about Daming.Let's complete some sentences about him.Daming is over 65 years old.He still works every day.He is thin and of average height.He is very fit.He is an elderly man.He is strong enough to control his raft in the river where he lives and works with his comrades.Thanks to these details, we have a vivid picture of him.However, in the passage, the writer has his own way of describing Daming.Let's complete these sentences.Although and but are used to show a sharp contrast.What does the writer want to show through the contrast?Please open your book.Turn to page 20.Read paragraph 1 and answer the question.You may say that Daming loves his work so much that he doesn't want to give up.Or the writer wants to show the comrades help him a lot and make his work much easier.So the writer describes Daming by using contrast in order to show his love to his work and the great convenience his comrades offer.Do you still remember what the comrades are like?Describe comrades according to the pictures.You may describe comrades like this.Comrades are large black birds.They have dark feathers, long necks, and large feet.They are fish eaters.They catch fish by diving, so they are excellent divers.First you introduce the definition.They are birds.Then you describe the appearance and their body parts.At last you may talk about his living skill.Thank you for your efforts.We have a clear picture in our mind.Does the writer describe comrades in the same way?Now let's read paragraph 2 again.Can we find the definition?And the living skill.So after reading this paragraph, we may feel amazed that the comrades are really good at swimming underwater and catching fish.Does the writer mention anything about the appearance?Only their large feet.Why does the writer write in this way?We know that their large feet are used to push them quickly through the water, which enables them to swim well underwater.That's why they are good at catching fish.Here we can see their large feet are the supporting details.They are provided to back up the main idea.Please read paragraph 2 and underline some other supporting details you find.They can dive deep down.And they can stay underwater for a long time.How deep can they dive down and how long can they stay underwater?25 meters and for up to 2 minutes.Up to here means as long as.The writer wants to show that they can stay underwater for such a long time.So these supporting details are used to make readers believe they are really good at catching fish.Still remember how comrades help diving to fish?As we mentioned in the previous lesson, verbs are very important.I wonder if you know the meanings of these verbs.Match the words and the phrase in column A with the meanings in column B.Let's check the answers.What's the meaning of set off?To start a journey.And reach?We should choose C.What's the meaning of swallow then?Still remember why daming ties a piece of grass around the neck of each bird?Because in this way, the fish cannot go down the bird's throats into their stomachs.So we choose F.And bang.We choose D.And number 5, hang, goes with the meaning e.And what about remove?Good.And can you use these words?Please fill in the blanks with verbs according to the pictures.That's task one on the worksheet.Well, let's check the answers.Picture A, tie a piece of grass around the neck of each bird.Picture B, remove the fish from the bird's mouth.Picture C, jump up and down and bend the water.And D, swim down and catch the fish.And bring them back to the raft.We have already known what they do.Please put the phrases into the right order and describe how daming catches fish with the comrades.These words and pictures may help
